title: Private Deployment: Customer KMS Integration Operator Guide — Outline + TODOs (WIP)
body:
Context
- This is an outline + TODO list for the Private deployment KMS integration operator guide.
- Target audience: customer operators + Redwood field/Solutions Eng supporting Private installs.
- Goal: make KMS setup repeatable and audit-friendly; minimize time-to-diagnosis for common failures (AccessDenied, wrong ARN, throttling, timeouts, key disabled).
- This doc will be migrated to Confluence + docs site after reviews.

Non-goals (call out early)
- Not a cryptography design doc.
- Not a full KMS primer (link out to cloud provider docs).
- Not covering Hosted API (Private only; may reference differences briefly).

Proposed information architecture (top-level sections)
1) Overview
   - What Redwood encrypts in Private deployments (high level): secrets, customer-provided credentials/config, control-plane metadata, etc. (confirm exact list w/ Security)
   - Envelope encryption model (KEK/DEK naming; avoid deep crypto)
   - Where KMS is used: control plane vs data plane (spell out which components call KMS)
   - Failure mode posture summary: what happens if KMS is slow/unavailable (degraded mode vs hard fail; align to ADR-007)

2) Prerequisites / Requirements
   - Required cloud provider: AWS / GCP / Azure (Private supports all three; confirm current GA status)
   - Network connectivity requirements:
     - Private cluster -> KMS endpoints (public or private endpoints)
     - DNS + firewall allowlists (include ports)
     - Proxy considerations (common in regulated environments)
   - Time sync (NTP) requirement (token signing/STS + request validity)
   - Regional constraints (KMS key region must match / or allowed cross-region? clarify)
   - Minimum permissions + separation of duties:
     - Runtime decrypt role/principal
     - Rotation/admin role/principal
     - Break-glass guidance (link to infra standard once published)

3) Configuration model in Redwood Private
   - Where operators configure KMS in Private:
     - Installer values file / Helm values / env vars (confirm exact config surfaces)
     - Key identifiers supported:
       - AWS KMS key ARN
       - GCP KMS key resource path
       - Azure Key Vault key ID/URL
   - Required config fields (table)
     - Provider
     - Region / location
     - Key ID
     - Auth method (role/identity)
     - Optional: timeouts/retry budgets (call out recommended defaults + guardrails)
   - Security notes:
     - Do not store plaintext credentials in Git
     - Use secrets manager / sealed secrets / external secret operator (if supported)

4) Provider-specific setup guides (core of the doc)
   4.1) AWS (most common)
     - Options for auth:
       - EKS IRSA (preferred)
       - EC2 instance profiles
       - Static access keys (discouraged; only for constrained environments)
     - Required IAM policy (least privilege)
       - kms:Decrypt, kms:Encrypt, kms:GenerateDataKey, kms:DescribeKey
       - kms:CreateGrant? (only if needed; confirm)
       - Condition keys: kms:ViaService, kms:CallerAccount, encryption context constraints (if applicable)
     - Key policy vs IAM policy (common pitfall)
     - Example IAM snippets (include redacted placeholders)
     - Example KMS key policy snippet for granting role access
     - Dedicated section: "Why AccessDenied happens even when the IAM policy looks right" (key policy, SCPs, permission boundaries)

   4.2) GCP
     - Workload Identity (preferred)
     - Service account key files (discouraged)
     - Required roles:
       - cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
       - cloudkms.viewer (if needed for Describe)
     - Key ring / crypto key / crypto key version model (explain in 3–5 bullets)
     - Example resource path formats

   4.3) Azure
     - Managed Identity (preferred)
     - Service principal (fallback)
     - Required Key Vault access:
       - get, wrapKey, unwrapKey (confirm exact permissions)
     - Key Vault network rules / private endpoints gotchas
     - Key versioning model (how rotations appear as new versions)

5) Installer preflight checks + validation report
   - Explain what the installer checks and when:
     - Valid key ID format
     - Permissions to call decrypt/encrypt / wrap/unwrap
     - Region/location mismatch detection
     - Rate limit / latency smoke test (if implemented)
   - What artifacts it produces:
     - Validation report file path (where output goes)
     - Recommended to attach to change ticket for audit evidence
   - TODO: add screenshots of installer output for:
     - Success
     - AccessDenied
     - Wrong key ID
     - Key disabled/scheduled for deletion
     - Region mismatch
   - Note: align wording with installer PR-392 output strings (avoid doc drift)

6) Key rotation in Private (operator workflow)
   - This should be concise and point to the full rotation runbook once finalized
   - Define terms:
     - KEK rotation vs DEK rotation (if customer asks)
     - "Dual-read/dual-decrypt window" concept (link ADR-008)
   - Operator responsibilities:
     - Create/enable new key version (provider-specific)
     - Update Redwood config to point to new key version OR allowlist additional version (depending on provider)
     - Rollout sequencing (control plane first, then data plane) (confirm w/ Platform)
     - Verification steps (logs/metrics to confirm decrypt success)
     - Cutover criteria and rollback triggers (high level; link to SRE runbook)
   - Evidence checklist (short): change ticket, key version IDs, timestamps, installer validation report, audit log export
   - TODO: get final language from Security/GRC (Olga Petrov / Daniel Carter)

7) Observability: dashboards, logs, alerts
   - Metrics operators should care about (by name once stable):
     - KMS latency (p50/p95/p99)
     - Error rate by taxonomy (AccessDenied, Throttling, Timeout, NotFound, InvalidCiphertext)
     - Circuit breaker state / open count (if exposed)
   - How to access in Private:
     - Where the dashboards live (Grafana?)
     - What labels/tags to filter by (cluster, service, region)
   - Logs
     - Example log lines and key fields (request_id, key_id, error_category)
     - Guidance: do NOT log plaintext or key material
   - Alerts
     - Recommended paging thresholds (initial defaults; tune per environment)
     - Noise notes: separate prod vs staging
   - TODO: add screenshots of the KMS health dashboard panels once the pack is finalized

8) Troubleshooting (table-driven)
   - Provide a "Symptom -> Likely cause -> Verification -> Fix" matrix.
   - Must include these known issues:
     - AccessDenied on decrypt
       - Cause: IAM role missing kms:Decrypt OR key policy missing principal OR permission boundary
       - Verify: CloudTrail / audit logs / installer preflight
       - Fix: update key policy + role binding
       - Link: SUP-19341
     - Throttling / rate exceeded
       - Cause: KMS quotas too low for workload; retry storm; burst traffic
       - Verify: throttle metrics, cloud provider KMS monitoring
       - Fix: tune retry budgets/backoff; request quota; enable caching/batching knobs where safe
       - Link: SUP-19377
     - Timeout spikes / intermittent 5xx
       - Cause: network path to KMS; KMS regional incident; overly aggressive timeouts
       - Verify: latency histograms; tracer spans
       - Fix: ensure private endpoints; check DNS; adjust timeout within guardrails
     - InvalidCiphertext / decrypt mismatch
       - Cause: wrong key ID after rotation; partial cutover; key material mismatch
       - Verify: look for key_version in logs; check config rollout status
       - Fix: rollback to previous key; re-enable dual-read window; redeploy
     - NotFound / wrong ARN or wrong location
     - Key disabled / scheduled deletion
     - Azure Key Vault firewall blocks
     - GCP Workload Identity misbinding
   - Include a short "collect these artifacts before escalating" checklist:
     - Installer validation report
     - Redacted config snippet
     - 15 min of metrics screenshots
     - 20–30 lines of relevant logs with request IDs

9) Security FAQ (short)
   - Who owns key material? (customer)
   - Can Redwood staff access plaintext? (expected: no; explain support boundaries)
   - How do we do break-glass? (process + time-boxed access; link to internal doc)
   - What happens during KMS outage? (expected behavior; availability vs strictness tradeoff)
   - Rotation cadence expectations (quarterly/annual; customer-driven)

10) Appendix
   - Glossary: KEK/DEK, envelope, key version, grant, IRSA, Workload Identity, managed identity
   - Provider docs links
   - Redwood support escalation paths
   - Change management template snippet (what to put in ticket)

Screenshots / diagrams needed (tracking list)
- Diagram: Private deployment components + where KMS is called (control plane vs data plane)
- AWS:
  - IAM role + policy example (console + Terraform)
  - KMS key policy example
  - CloudTrail event example for a failed Decrypt (AccessDenied)
- Installer preflight:
  - Success
  - AccessDenied
  - Wrong key identifier
  - Throttling warning (if present)
- Observability:
  - KMS dashboard main panels
  - Example trace span for KMS call
- Troubleshooting:
  - Example "actionable error" surfaced to operator (permission denied remediation hints)

Example configs to include (sanitized)
- values.yaml snippet for Private installer (AWS/GCP/Azure variants)
- Terraform snippets:
  - AWS KMS key + policy + IRSA role
  - GCP KMS key ring + crypto key + IAM binding
  - Azure Key Vault + key + access policy / RBAC
- NOTE: use placeholders: <ACCOUNT_ID>, <PROJECT_ID>, <TENANT_ID>, <CLUSTER_NAME>, <NAMESPACE>

Known pitfalls / operator "gotchas" (callouts to include as warning boxes)
- KMS key policy vs IAM policy mismatch (AWS)
- SCP/permission boundaries overriding otherwise-correct IAM
- Region mismatch: key in us-east-1 but cluster in us-west-2 (or private endpoint pointing wrong)
- Azure Key Vault networking: private endpoint required but DNS not configured
- GCP Workload Identity: service account annotation wrong; token audience mismatch
- Rotation cutover partial state (some pods using old key id, some new) if rollout isn’t sequenced
- Over-tuning retries: can amplify KMS load; follow retry budget defaults

Open questions (assign owners)
- Exact list of Redwood components in Private that call KMS directly vs via control plane (Owner: Benji Okafor)
- Are cross-region KMS calls supported/allowed? If allowed, any latency/SLO guidance? (Owner: Sean Gallagher)
- Do we require separate principals for rotation vs runtime decrypt in Private docs? (Owner: Jordan Lee)
- Confirm exact permissions list for Azure (wrap/unwrap vs encrypt/decrypt semantics) (Owner: Hanae Suzuki)
- Where does the installer store the validation report and what’s the stable filename? (Owner: Bruno Silva)
- Final stance on "degraded mode" during KMS issues in Private (hard fail vs allow cached?) (Owner: Marcus Lin + Ethan Park)

Review plan
- Round 1: Private deployments + installer (Vivek, Bruno)
- Round 2: Security/Compliance (Hanae, Marcus, Olga)
- Round 3: SRE (Sean, Rafael) — ensure troubleshooting + alerts are accurate
- Final: Docs IA + publish checklist (Elliot Price)

Next steps (TODO)
- Convert outline into first draft narrative text (Kira)
- Pull exact config key names and defaults from code to avoid drift (Bruno)
- Add troubleshooting matrix based on real tickets + incident threads (Kira + Sean)
- Draft provider-specific examples and get Security sign-off on permission scopes (Jordan + Hanae)
- Collect screenshots in a staging Private environment and store in a shared folder (Vivek)
- After approval, migrate to Confluence and then docs site PR
